title: Review: Elastic strain energy; Gas laws and ideal gas equation; Temperature, internal energy, thermal equilibrium; Kinetic theory of gases; Specific heat capacity and latent heat; Angular measures and uniform circular motion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: C01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; C01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; T01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; C01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C01-1#N.4a, MT03-1#N.11, T01-1#N.2, T02-1#N.3a, T02-uk1#N.10b, T05-1#N.2a, T06-1#N.14, T06-uk1#N.11, C01-1#N.12a, MT03-1#N.8, T01-1#N.11, T02-1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Period
items.clue: Time taken for one full revolution.

items.label: Frequency
items.clue: Number of revolutions each second, measured in Hz.

items.label: Thermal equilibrium
items.clue: Condition of bodies in contact with no net energy transfer between them.

items.label: Centripetal acceleration
items.clue: Rate of change of velocity in circular motion, pointing inward, of size v²/r.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel of diameter 0.700 m rotates at a steady rate about a fixed axle, making one complete revolution every 0.250 s. What is the linear speed of a point on the rim of the wheel?
A spring obeys Hooke's law. When it is compressed by 3.0 cm it stores 0.45 J. How much energy does it store when it is compressed by 4.5 cm?
questions.explanation: Energy ∝ (compression)². The compression is 1.5 times larger, so E = 0.45 × 1.5² = 1.0 J.

questions.stem: A 0.20 kg copper block at 80 °C is lowered into a large tank containing 200 kg of water at 20 °C. The water has far more internal energy than the block. Which statement describes the resultant thermal energy transfer?

options.text: From the block to the water, until they reach the same temperature.
From the water to the block, since the water has more internal energy.
Coldness passes from the water into the block, so the block cools down.
From the block to the water, until they have equal internal energies.

questions.stem: An electric kettle heats 250 g of water from 18 °C to 90 °C. The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 × 10³ J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. How much energy is transferred to the water? Ignore energy transferred to the kettle and surroundings.

A student uses the electrical method to find the specific heat capacity of a brass block. Her value is 10% higher than the data-book value. Which change to her method would most reduce this difference?

options.text: Repeat the experiment three times and calculate a mean value
Use a thermometer with a finer scale, reading to 0.1 °C
Wrap the block in thick insulation and put a lid of insulation on top
Use a lower heater power so the block heats more slowly

questions.explanation: Less energy escapes to the surroundings, so more of VIt raises the block's temperature. The value of c falls towards the true one.

questions.stem: A cylinder contains 0.64 kg of oxygen gas, which consists of O₂ molecules. The molar mass of oxygen atoms is 16 g mol⁻¹, and N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. How many oxygen molecules are in the cylinder?

A container holds a mixture of hydrogen (H₂) and oxygen (O₂) at one temperature. An oxygen molecule has 16 times the mass of a hydrogen molecule. What is (rms speed of the hydrogen molecules)/(rms speed of the oxygen molecules)?

options.text: 1, because the two gases are at the same temperature.
16, because the hydrogen molecules have 1/16 of the mass.
1/4, because the heavier molecules hit harder and so move faster.
4, because equal mean kinetic energies mean speed ∝ 1/√m.

questions.explanation: ½m(rms speed)², the mean kinetic energy, depends only on T, so it is the same for both, so rms speed ∝ 1/√m = √16 = 4.

questions.stem: Two sealed containers of equal volume are at the same temperature. Each holds the same number N of molecules of an ideal gas. Each molecule of gas Y has 4 times the mass of a molecule of gas X. What is (pressure of Y)/(pressure of X)?

options.text: 4, because pV = ⅓Nm × (mean square speed) and m is 4 times as large.
1, because m × (mean square speed) is the same for both gases at the same temperature.
¼, because the heavier molecules move more slowly and hit the walls less often.
2, because the molecules of Y have half the rms speed and 4 times the mass.

questions.explanation: Same T → same mean translational KE, so m × (mean square speed) is equal. With equal N and V, pV = ⅓Nm × (mean square speed) gives equal pressures (as pV = NkT says).

questions.stem: The drum of a washing machine has a diameter of 0.50 m. It rotates about a horizontal axis at constant speed, with a time period of 0.050 s. What is the centripetal acceleration of a sock pressed against the inside of the drum?

The spring in a toy dart launcher has a spring constant of 400 N m⁻¹. It is compressed by 0.030 m and then released, firing a dart of mass 0.012 kg horizontally. All the elastic potential energy is transferred to the dart's kinetic energy. What is the speed of the dart?

options.text: 7.7 m s⁻¹
5.5 m s⁻¹
30 m s⁻¹
3.9 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A thermometer at room temperature, 20 °C, is placed in a cup of water at 70 °C. Its reading rises for a while and then stays steady. Why does the steady reading give the temperature of the water?

options.text: All energy transfer between the thermometer and the water has then stopped completely for good.
The thermometer then has as much internal energy as the water in the cup, so the two readings match.
The cold in the thermometer has then all flowed out into the water, so it can read correctly.
They are then in thermal equilibrium, so no net energy is transferred between them.

questions.stem: 0.20 kg of water and 0.20 kg of cooking oil, both at 20 °C, are each supplied with 12 kJ of energy. Specific heat capacities: water 4180 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, oil 2000 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. Assume no energy is lost. Which statement about their final temperatures is correct?

options.text: The oil ends at 50 °C and the water at about 34 °C.
The water ends at 50 °C and the oil at about 34 °C.
They end at the same temperature, as each gets 12 kJ.
The oil ends at 30 °C and the water at about 14 °C.
